sentences: Graph diameter becomes expensive when a geometric intersection graph has many implicit edges.
This conjecture proposes bounded VC dimension of the relevant distance neighborhoods as a sufficient structural condition for truly subquadratic diameter-threshold algorithms.
The geometric objects should have low descriptive complexity, but their ambient dimension need not be two.
The source's examples suggest a common explanation for several otherwise separate algorithmic successes.
The task is to turn that observed relationship between set-system structure and distance computation into a general theorem.
